title: NimRTC Profile Schema v1.2
description: Scenario assembly profile (v1.2 — adds the `video` block per docs/plan/remote-desktop-plan.md). Strictly ADDITIVE on top of v1.1: every v1.0/v1.1 profile loads unchanged; v1.2 profiles add the `video` top-level key. The C++ loader (src/modules/assembly/src/assembly.cpp) reads the block into `assembly::VideoSection`. The `video` block is what makes a *screen* stream expressible: content type, codec preference table, hardware-backend policy, ladder mode and the resolution floor, plus the colour range / matrix the compositor actually produces.

video.description: v1.2 additive block — describes the *shape* of the outgoing video stream. A camera stream leaves this block empty (the default) and behaves exactly as it did in v1.1. A screen stream fills it in.

codec_name.description: Pin one codec (e.g. "h264", "h265", "av1"). Empty = pick from `codec_preference`.

codec_preference.description: Ordered codec preference table. The encoder walks it in order and takes the first codec that is actually available on this machine AND permitted by `codec_backend`. The screen-content table is ["av1", "h265", "h264"] — AV1's intra-frame coding dominates on flat, sharp-edged text; H.265 is the safe hardware fallback; H.264 is the universal fallback.

codec_backend.description: Backend policy for the video encoder. 'auto' = hardware first, software as a fallback (remote-desktop plan B2). The authoritative parser is the codec seam's `codec_backend_from_string`; this schema lists the accepted spellings but does not enforce the runtime availability.

content_type.description: What the encoder is looking at. 'screen' enables the screen-content coding tools (no temporal prediction on flat regions, sharper intra). 'motion' is a camera. 'text' is pure text/scroll.

ladder_mode.description: How the resolution ladder spends its budget. 'quality' keeps the resolution high and lets the frame rate drop (correct for screen content: legibility first). 'smoothness' is the opposite (correct for a camera). 'fixed' disables the ladder.

resolution_floor.description: The ladder never crosses below this resolution. Configurable because the right value depends on the machine class: 1080p on a hardware-encoding box, 720p on a software-only one. Written as [width, height]; an object form {width, height} is also accepted by the loader.

pixel_format.description: The pixel format the encoder is fed with, before its own internal conversion.

color_range.description: The colour range of the source. A desktop compositor produces FULL range; a camera usually produces LIMITED. Getting this wrong looks like 'the codec is broken' (washed-out blacks or crushed highlights).

color_matrix.description: The YUV matrix of the source. bt709 is the correct default for sRGB desktop content.
